failures.message: sherpa_onnx.OfflineTts.generate() segfaults (native crash, exit code 139) using the sriram09764/itantra-tts-onnx community sherpa-onnx VITS export for Telugu, with sherpa-onnx 1.13.8 on Windows CPU. Model construction/loading succeeds; the crash is inside synthesis and is reproducible even with a single trivial Telugu word ('నమస్తే'), ruling out a text-length or punctuation issue. A separate community ONNX export of the same underlying facebook/mms-tts-tel checkpoint (willwade/mms-tts-multilingual-models-onnx) loads and synthesizes correctly via plain onnxruntime, so the failure is specific to this conversion or to sherpa-onnx's VITS runner expectations for it, not to the environment or the base model.

Both Vakyansh Telugu Glow-TTS voices require compiling the repo's monotonic_align Cython extension (src/glow_tts/monotonic_align, a setup.py build_ext step) before inference can run. This machine has no C compiler (no cl.exe/MSVC, no gcc), and the system drive (C:) had only about 3GB free at the time, which is too little to safely install Visual Studio Build Tools (typically several GB). Rather than risk filling the system drive for an uncertain build, this was recorded as a failure and the family was skipped. The checkpoints themselves (glow.zip x2, shared hifi.zip vocoder) were verified to exist and download correctly (HTTP 200, correct sizes) at storage.googleapis.com/vakyansh-open-models; this is purely a local build-toolchain gap, not a problem with the model or the checkpoint URLs.
